scope: Daily full-universe research refresh across existing Power Stack categories and US, Hong Kong/China and Malaysia. Research/data only; no site code or scoring logic changes.
decision: No additional stock promotion or formal conviction change cleared the bar after the unusually large Aug 24 adjacent-theme expansion.

macro.marketRead: Aug 24 US session weakened in semiconductors/AI while financials held up. The S&P 500 fell 0.28% and Nasdaq 0.76% in reported closing data; oil fell about 2.4% to roughly $85/bbl while gold rose and long-end rates remain restrictive. This reinforces valuation discipline rather than invalidating physical AI/grid demand.
macro.aiCapexRead: Political/grid resistance to data-centre expansion and investor concern about debt-funded AI capex are now explicit market risks. Prefer contracted/backlog-rich physical bottlenecks and cash-generative suppliers over narrative-only duration.
macro.oilRead: Crude eased despite Iran sanctions headlines; keep refined-product logistics/refiners tactical rather than upgrading generic upstream beta solely on geopolitics.

ism.status: July 2026 remains latest official data as of Aug 25. Manufacturing August data due Sep 1; Services August data due Sep 3.
ism.interpretation: Electrical/electronic scarcity, low customer inventories and elevated prices still support equipment/networking/power reliability and first-wave automation; no new ISM release exists today.

categoryReads.Power / Grid: Still highest-quality core category. Aug 24 additions BDC/GNRC broaden the stack into networking and behind-the-meter reliability; do not chase stretched small electrical names after sharp rallies.
categoryReads.AI / Data centres: HBM/advanced packaging and networking remain the freshest differentiated bottlenecks. AI financing/debt and political/grid constraints increase the value of real orders, customer funding and installed capacity.
categoryReads.Nuclear: No fresh evidence today warrants changing BWXT/CEG/1816.HK hierarchy or speculative treatment of pre-commercial reactor developers.
categoryReads.Uranium / Fuel: No new catalyst today changes CCJ/LEU core plus NXE higher-beta satellite framework.
categoryReads.Oil & Gas: Oil pullback argues against broad upgrades. Maintain integrated majors/core infrastructure and tactical refinery/product-tanker expressions where product scarcity is the actual thesis.
categoryReads.Metals: Copper remains preferred structural metal; high rates and China/global-cycle sensitivity argue against indiscriminate miner additions.
categoryReads.Robotics / Automation: Commercialisation order unchanged: warehouse/fixed industrial automation first; cobots/mobile manipulation second; industrial humanoids third; open-world/general-purpose robots last. Machine vision/networking remain form-factor-agnostic picks-and-shovels.
categoryReads.Malaysia: No new core name cleared the quality/valuation bar. Powerwell's sharp rally and analyst downgrade reinforce entry-price discipline; retain existing TNB/SCGBHD/YTLPOWR/SunCon/MN/CBHB hierarchy rather than forcing a new ticker.
categoryReads.Hong Kong / China: ASMPT remains the strongest new differentiated Aug 24 candidate. No additional China/HK name cleared the bar today.

existingUniverseReview: Existing theses were re-screened for current macro/valuation/category evidence. No thesis break or evidence strong enough for a formal conviction change was identified today; Aug 24 BDC/GNRC/AMKR/0522.HK additions remain the priority follow-up queue, with STNG/1138.HK tactical.

watch.reason: Utility-scale solar resilience and US supply-chain positioning are interesting, but it is less differentiated versus existing Power Stack grid/generation exposures and needs a full valuation/order-book pass before inclusion.

rejectedToday.reason: Already crowded and less differentiated than packaging/networking/power bottlenecks.
Strong demand is increasingly reflected in price; avoid promoting on momentum alone.

researchGaps: Re-price BDC/GNRC/AMKR/0522.HK after the next earnings/technical reset rather than immediately increasing conviction.
Track Nvidia earnings for evidence on HBM/system pricing and capex durability.
Track US political/grid constraints on new data centres for implications across merchant power versus behind-the-meter reliability.
Next official ISM refresh is Sep 1 Manufacturing, then Sep 3 Services.
